question: Should the repository accept the new `maxPromptBytes` default and specialized-ownership rules as the compatibility contract for existing monorepo mappings after representative real-workspace evidence is supplied?
rationale: The code changes how existing repositories are sliced and how much source reaches reviews; automated tests do not establish whether that tradeoff is acceptable for current users.

options.title: Require representative proof
options.body: Keep the PR in review until it includes redacted before-and-after `clawpatch map` output or mapped-state artifacts showing the intended ownership and prompt omissions on a large monorepo.

options.title: Accept the bounded-context tradeoff
options.body: Approve the new cap and grouping behavior as the intended default after a mapper owner explicitly accepts possible reduced context for oversized reviews.

options.title: Narrow the behavior
options.body: Retain the bug fixes but avoid changing existing default coverage unless users opt into the prompt budget.

recommendation.title: Require representative proof
recommendation.body: Keep the PR in review until it includes redacted before-and-after `clawpatch map` output or mapped-state artifacts showing the intended ownership and prompt omissions on a large monorepo.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current mapper-focused implementation and can provide the requested representative proof, while final compatibility acceptance still needs repository review.
